hook: A year-end campaign won't save a message that was unclear all year.
direction: Angle: orgs scramble to launch giving campaigns in November without fixing the foggy message underneath. Contrarian take: the campaign is downstream of the clarity. If people don't know what you do or why it matters, urgency won't close the gap. Cover: what to fix first. Graphic: ig-native — short, wry, like a note typed in the app.

facebook.text:
A year-end campaign won't save a message that was unclear all year.

Every November, organizations scramble to build giving campaigns. New graphics, urgent copy, countdown timers. And underneath it all: a message nobody could explain clearly in March.

The campaign is downstream of the clarity. Urgency doesn't close a gap that confusion opened. If people don't know what you do or why it matters, a deadline won't change that.

Fix the message first. Who you serve, why it matters, what you're asking people to join. Then build the campaign on top of something solid.

instagram.text:
A year-end campaign won't save a message that was unclear all year.

Every November, orgs scramble: new graphics, urgent copy, countdown timers. But the campaign sits on top of whatever clarity (or fog) was already there.

If people couldn't explain what you do in March, a deadline won't fix that in December.

Fix the message first. Who you serve. Why it matters. What you're asking people to join. Then build the campaign on something solid.
